ja: 水星は太陽にいちばん近い惑星。大気がほとんどないため、昼は約430℃、夜は約−180℃まで温度が変わる。
easy: Mercury is the closest planet to the sun. It is about 430°C in the day and −180°C at night.
std: Mercury, the planet closest to the Sun, has almost no atmosphere, so temperatures swing from about 430°C by day to −180°C at night.

ja: 金星は太陽系でいちばん熱い惑星。厚い二酸化炭素の大気が熱を閉じ込め、表面は約460℃にもなる。
easy: Venus is the hottest planet. Its thick air traps heat, and the ground is about 460°C.
std: Venus is the hottest planet in the solar system; its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat, keeping the surface around 460°C.

ja: 火星には太陽系最大の火山オリンポス山がある。高さは約22kmで、エベレストの2倍以上。
easy: Mars has the biggest volcano in the solar system. It is about 22 km high.
std: Mars is home to Olympus Mons, the largest volcano in the solar system, about 22 kilometers high—more than twice the height of Everest.

ja: 木星の1日（自転の周期）は約10時間で、太陽系の惑星の中でいちばん短い。
easy: A day on Jupiter is only about 10 hours long, the shortest of all the planets.
std: Jupiter spins faster than any other planet, completing one rotation in about 10 hours.

ja: 土星の環の大部分は氷のかけらでできている。直径は数十万kmに広がるのに、厚さはとても薄い。
easy: Saturn's rings are mostly made of pieces of ice. They are very wide but very thin.
std: Saturn's rings are made mostly of chunks of water ice; they span hundreds of thousands of kilometers yet are extremely thin.

ja: 人の体はおよそ37兆個の細胞でできているという推定がある（2013年の研究）。
easy: One study says the human body has about 37 trillion cells.
std: A 2013 study estimated that the human body contains about 37 trillion cells.

ja: 人は1分間に15〜20回ほどまばたきをする。集中して画面を見ていると回数が減り、目が乾きやすくなる。
easy: People blink about 15 to 20 times a minute. We blink less when we look at screens.
std: People blink around 15 to 20 times a minute, but blink less while concentrating on screens, which can dry the eyes.

ja: 髪の毛は1か月に約1〜1.5cm伸びる。
easy: Hair grows about 1 to 1.5 centimeters a month.
std: Scalp hair grows roughly one to one and a half centimeters per month.

ja: 大人の体の血液は約5リットルで、体重のおよそ7〜8％にあたる。
easy: An adult has about 5 liters of blood.
std: An adult has about five liters of blood, roughly 7 to 8 percent of body weight.

ja: 大人は1日に約2万回呼吸している。
easy: Adults breathe about 20,000 times a day.
std: An adult breathes roughly 20,000 times a day at rest.

ja: 古代オリンピックは紀元前776年にギリシャのオリンピアで始まったと伝えられる。最初の競技は短距離走だけだった。
easy: The ancient Olympic Games began in Greece in 776 BC. The first event was a short running race.
std: The ancient Olympic Games are traditionally dated to 776 BC at Olympia, Greece, and at first featured only a short foot race.

ja: 近代オリンピックは、フランスのクーベルタンの呼びかけで1896年にアテネで始まった。
easy: The modern Olympics started in Athens in 1896, thanks to a Frenchman named Coubertin.
std: The modern Olympic Games began in Athens in 1896, inspired by the French educator Pierre de Coubertin.

ja: 五輪のマークの5つの輪は、5つの大陸のつながりを表す。白地と5色で、当時の世界の国旗の色がすべて描けるとされた。
easy: The five Olympic rings stand for five continents joined together.
std: The five Olympic rings represent the union of five continents; together with the white background, their colors were said to appear in every national flag of the time.

ja: 聖火リレーが始まったのは1936年のベルリン大会から。
easy: The Olympic torch relay started at the 1936 Berlin Games.
std: The Olympic torch relay was first held for the 1936 Berlin Games.

ja: 1964年の東京オリンピックはアジアで初めての大会。開会に合わせて東海道新幹線が開業した。
easy: The 1964 Tokyo Olympics were the first in Asia. The bullet train started just before them.
std: The 1964 Tokyo Olympics were the first held in Asia, and the Tokaido Shinkansen opened just in time for the Games.

ja: コーヒーの木の原産地はエチオピア。ヤギがコーヒーの実を食べて元気になったのを見て発見されたという伝説がある。
easy: Coffee plants come from Ethiopia. A story says goats ate the berries and became very lively.
std: Coffee originated in Ethiopia; legend says a goatherd discovered it after noticing his goats became energetic after eating the berries.

ja: 15世紀ごろ、イエメンでコーヒーが飲まれるようになった。積み出し港の名前「モカ」は今もコーヒーの名前に残る。
easy: People in Yemen drank coffee in the 1400s. The port of Mocha gave its name to a kind of coffee.
std: By the 15th century coffee was being drunk in Yemen; the port of Mocha, which shipped it, still lends its name to coffee drinks.

ja: 17世紀のロンドンのコーヒーハウスは、1杯の値段で議論や情報交換ができたため「ペニー大学」と呼ばれた。
easy: In the 1600s, London coffee houses were called 'penny universities'. For one penny, you could learn and talk.
std: Seventeenth-century London coffeehouses were nicknamed 'penny universities' because the price of a coffee bought access to news and debate.

ja: 日本には江戸時代に長崎の出島を通じてコーヒーが伝わった。本格的に広まったのは明治以降。
easy: Coffee came to Japan through Nagasaki in the Edo period. It became popular after 1868.
std: Coffee reached Japan through the Dutch trading post at Dejima in Nagasaki during the Edo period, but spread widely only after the Meiji era began.

ja: 缶コーヒーは1969年に日本で発売されたものが世界で最初期の一つとされる。
easy: Canned coffee was first sold in Japan in 1969.
std: Canned coffee was popularized in Japan, with one of the earliest products launched in 1969.

ja: 知られている最古の文字の一つは、約5000年前のメソポタミアの楔形文字。粘土板に葦のペンで刻んだ。
easy: One of the oldest kinds of writing is cuneiform, from about 5,000 years ago. People pressed it into clay.
std: Cuneiform, pressed into clay tablets with a reed stylus in Mesopotamia about 5,000 years ago, is among the oldest known writing systems.

ja: 古代エジプトのヒエログリフ（聖刻文字）は、1822年にシャンポリオンがロゼッタ・ストーンなどを手がかりに解読した。
easy: Egyptian hieroglyphs were understood again in 1822, with help from the Rosetta Stone.
std: Egyptian hieroglyphs were deciphered by Jean-François Champollion in 1822, using the Rosetta Stone among other sources.

ja: 地中海の商人だったフェニキア人の文字は、子音だけを表す22文字のアルファベット。多くの文字の祖先になった。
easy: The Phoenicians were traders. Their alphabet of 22 letters became the parent of many alphabets.
std: The Phoenician alphabet, 22 letters representing consonants, spread with Mediterranean traders and became the ancestor of many scripts.

ja: ギリシャ人はフェニキア文字を取り入れ、母音を表す文字を加えた。母音と子音を両方書く最初のアルファベットとされる。
easy: The Greeks took the Phoenician letters and added vowels.
std: The Greeks adapted the Phoenician script and added letters for vowels, creating what is often called the first true alphabet.

ja: 英語のアルファベットはラテン文字。J・U・W は、中世以降に区別されるようになった比較的新しい文字。
easy: English uses the Latin alphabet. The letters J, U, and W were added quite late.
std: English uses the Latin alphabet; J, U and W became distinct letters relatively late, from the Middle Ages onward.

ja: 数を記録した最古級の道具の一つは、約2万年前の骨に刻み目をつけた「イシャンゴの骨」（アフリカ・コンゴで発見）。
easy: One of the oldest counting tools is a bone with marks on it, from about 20,000 years ago.
std: The Ishango bone, a notched bone found in Congo and dated to about 20,000 years ago, is one of the oldest known counting tools.

ja: 今使われている0〜9の数字は「アラビア数字」と呼ばれるが、もとはインドで生まれ、アラビアを経てヨーロッパに広まった。
easy: Our numbers 0 to 9 are called 'Arabic numerals', but they started in India.
std: The digits 0–9 are called Arabic numerals but originated in India, reaching Europe through the Arab world.

ja: イタリアのフィボナッチは1202年の本でインド・アラビア数字をヨーロッパに紹介した。ローマ数字より計算がずっと楽だった。
easy: In 1202, Fibonacci wrote a book that brought Arabic numerals to Europe.
std: Fibonacci's 1202 book Liber Abaci introduced Hindu-Arabic numerals to Europe, making calculation far easier than with Roman numerals.

ja: 負の数は古代中国の数学書『九章算術』で使われていた。ヨーロッパでは長い間「ありえない数」と考えられた。
easy: Negative numbers were used in ancient China. In Europe, people did not accept them for a long time.
std: Negative numbers appear in the ancient Chinese text The Nine Chapters on the Mathematical Art, while European mathematicians resisted them for centuries.

ja: 等号「＝」は1557年にイギリスのロバート・レコードが考えた。「2本の平行線ほど等しいものはない」からだという。
easy: The equals sign '=' was invented in 1557 by Robert Recorde.
std: The equals sign was introduced by Welsh mathematician Robert Recorde in 1557, who chose two parallel lines because 'no two things can be more equal'.

ja: 1488年、ポルトガルのディアスがアフリカ南端の喜望峰を回った。
easy: In 1488, Bartolomeu Dias sailed around the southern tip of Africa.
std: In 1488 the Portuguese explorer Bartolomeu Dias rounded the Cape of Good Hope at Africa's southern tip.

ja: 1492年、コロンブスは西回りでアジアを目指してカリブ海の島に着いた。本人は最後までアジアの近くだと考えていたとされる。
easy: In 1492, Columbus reached islands in the Caribbean. He thought he was near Asia.
std: In 1492 Columbus reached the Caribbean while seeking a western route to Asia, and reportedly believed to the end that he had reached Asia's edge.

ja: 1498年、ヴァスコ・ダ・ガマがインドに到達し、ヨーロッパからアフリカを回ってアジアへ行く航路が開かれた。
easy: In 1498, Vasco da Gama reached India by sailing around Africa.
std: In 1498 Vasco da Gama reached India, opening a sea route from Europe to Asia around Africa.

ja: マゼランの船団は1519年に出発し、1522年に初の世界一周を果たした。マゼラン本人は途中のフィリピンで戦死した。
easy: Magellan's ships were the first to sail around the world, from 1519 to 1522. Magellan himself died on the way.
std: Magellan's expedition, which set out in 1519, completed the first circumnavigation in 1522, though Magellan himself was killed in the Philippines.

ja: 1543年、ポルトガル人を乗せた船が種子島に着き、日本に鉄砲が伝わった。
easy: In 1543, Portuguese people arrived at Tanegashima and brought guns to Japan.
std: In 1543 a ship carrying Portuguese traders landed on Tanegashima, introducing firearms to Japan.

ja: 水深200mより深い「深海」は、地球の表面のおよそ3分の2を占めている。
easy: The deep sea, below 200 meters, covers about two-thirds of Earth's surface.
std: The deep sea, generally defined as below 200 meters, covers about two-thirds of Earth's surface.

ja: 深海の水圧はとても高い。水深約1万mでは、指先ほどの面積に1トン以上の重さがかかるのと同じ。
easy: The deep sea has very strong water pressure. At 10,000 meters, it is like one ton on your fingertip.
std: Pressure in the deepest ocean exceeds 1,000 times that at the surface—more than a tonne on every square centimeter.

ja: ダイオウイカが生きた姿で初めて撮影されたのは2004年で、日本の研究者による。
easy: A living giant squid was first photographed in 2004 by Japanese scientists.
std: The first photographs of a live giant squid in its natural habitat were taken in 2004 by Japanese researchers.

ja: 深海の熱水噴出孔のまわりでは、太陽の光に頼らず、化学物質からエネルギーを得る生き物の生態系がある。
easy: Near hot vents in the deep sea, living things get energy from chemicals, not sunlight.
std: Around deep-sea hydrothermal vents, entire ecosystems rely on chemosynthesis rather than sunlight for energy.

ja: 海底は、月の表面よりも詳しい地図が作られていないと言われる。
easy: We have better maps of the Moon than of the bottom of our oceans.
std: Much of the ocean floor has been mapped in less detail than the surface of the Moon.

ja: エビングハウスの研究では、覚えた内容は最初の1日で急速に忘れられる。「忘却曲線」と呼ばれる。
easy: We forget new things very quickly, especially on the first day. This is the 'forgetting curve'.
std: Hermann Ebbinghaus showed that newly learned material is forgotten rapidly at first, especially within the first day: the 'forgetting curve'.

ja: 間隔をあけて繰り返し復習すると、一度にまとめて覚えるより長く記憶に残る。「分散学習」の効果。
easy: Studying a little at a time, with breaks between, helps you remember longer.
std: Spacing out review sessions over time leads to longer-lasting memory than cramming, a finding known as the spacing effect.

ja: 人が一度に覚えておける項目の数は、かつて「7±2」と言われたが、今は4つ前後とする研究が多い。
easy: People can hold only a few things in mind at once, maybe about four.
std: Working memory was once said to hold 'seven plus or minus two' items, but more recent research suggests about four.

ja: 「記憶の宮殿」は、覚えたいものをよく知っている場所に置いていくように想像する記憶術。古代ギリシャから伝わる。
easy: The 'memory palace' is a trick: you imagine putting things in places you know well.
std: The 'memory palace', or method of loci, places items to be remembered along an imagined familiar route, a technique dating back to ancient Greece.

ja: 人に教えるつもりで学ぶと、よりよく理解し覚えられるという研究がある。「教えることによる学習」と呼ばれる。
easy: If you study as if you will teach it, you remember it better.
std: Studies suggest that learning with the expectation of teaching others improves understanding and recall, a phenomenon called learning by teaching.
